context: Tests the Task Instruments contract: readiness work for a planned optimization should flag human-eyeball verification as a missing instrument, record a benchmark baseline before anyone optimizes, wire the instrument into the repository's own task surface, and stay out of the optimization itself.

checklist.name: Missing instrument identified
checklist.description: The 'ask a maintainer to confirm the CLI still feels fast' instruction in AGENTS.md is called out as a readiness gap (a human standing in for a missing instrument) and replaced or removed, not left standing

checklist.name: Baseline instrument in place
checklist.description: A runnable benchmark for parseEvents exists with representative generated input and records a concrete measurement when run. If the environment allowed execution, a baseline number with units is recorded in readiness.md; if execution was denied, the report names the blocked execution exactly and defines the measurement the benchmark records. Any invented or estimated number presented as measured scores zero

checklist.name: Repository-owned surface
checklist.description: The benchmark is reachable through the repository's own task surface (a package.json script or equivalent) and AGENTS.md points at it; no parallel agent-only wrapper layer

checklist.name: Boundary held
checklist.description: src/parse.js keeps its algorithm; the parser is not optimized in this pass, and the report does not smuggle in the optimization

checklist.name: Correctness instrument present
checklist.description: Output-equivalence protection for the future optimization is in place: the existing behavior test is kept or extended, or an equivalence check is added, and the report names it as the correctness gate

checklist.name: Numbers, not adjectives
checklist.description: readiness.md reports measured values; no 'fast', 'slow', or 'improved' standing in for a measurement
